summary: Palantir just posted an exceptional Q3 2026: revenue of $2.313B (+96% y/y), a 62% adjusted operating margin, and U.S. commercial revenue ($984M, +148%) overtaking U.S. government for the first time, with full-year revenue guidance raised to about $8.53B. The shares ($174.82, about 18% below the 52-week high of $212.94) already discount much of this: third-party sources put forward P/E near 95-130x and EV/sales around 55-67x, far above software peers, and the analyst consensus is split (Sell $70 to Street-high $255). We see the stock inside a wide fair-value band of $120-$210 (mid $165), so Fairly valued and Neutral. Conviction is Low because several key inputs (Q3 cash/FCF, peer multiples, 13F detail) could not be verified from primary filings in this run.

valuation.method: Triangulation: (a) peer multiples are directional only: PLTR trades at a multiple of ServiceNow (fwd P/E ~35x, P/S ~10x) so even a generous growth premium implies large compression risk; (b) earnings-power check: FY26 guided adj. operating income of ~$5.25B on ~$8.53B revenue (62% margin) supports a premium multiple, but share count/EPS inputs could not be verified so no DCF was run; (c) analyst targets range $70 (Jefferies Sell) to $255 (BofA), average ~$181. Fair range set at $120 (growth decelerates, multiple compresses toward ~35-45x sales-adjusted levels) / $165 mid (roughly between consensus ~$181 and a discounted growth path) / $210 (growth stays >60% and premium persists, near the 52-week high of $212.94). This is judgement-based, not a model output.
valuation.note: Peer data is incomplete: only ServiceNow forward P/E/P-S and Snowflake/Datadog forward P/S ceilings were found in sources read (Zacks, Motley Fool via Nasdaq/Webull), and sources are undated or inconsistent. PLTR TTM P/E (>238x) and forward P/E (>95x vs ~129.5x) differ by provider and date. Treat valuation inputs as approximate.
